seo_title: Cost of Living in Samui 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live on Samui per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A tropical island in the Gulf of Thailand: visa-free for 60 days, with beaches and palm trees year-round. Calmer and greener than Phuket, convenient to live on under the DTV visa, but everything imported is a bit pricier than on the mainland, and healthcare and logistics are island-style.
pros: Visa-free for 60 days, convenient to live on under the DTV visa
Tropics year-round: beaches, palms, a warm sea
Well-developed infrastructure for expats and great food
A large Russian-speaking and digital-nomad community
cons: Everything imported is slightly pricier than on the mainland
Island healthcare and logistics — for anything complex people go to Bangkok
You need a scooter: there's almost no public transport

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Up to 60 days without a visa for Russians, with the option to extend by 30 days at the immigration office.

visa_steps.title: DTV visa (for long-term living)
visa_steps.description: A 5-year multi-entry visa for remote workers — up to 180 days per entry without leaving.

visa_steps.title: Renting a home
visa_steps.description: Villas and condos are rented monthly; prices and demand are higher during the winter high season.

visa_steps.title: Account and connectivity
visa_steps.description: A local SIM card with a large data plan; a Thai bank account is possible with a visa and an address.

visa_steps.title: Transport
visa_steps.description: Renting a scooter is the main way to get around; you'll need an international driving licence.

faq.question: Do Russian citizens need a visa for Samui?
faq.answer: No, visa-free for up to 60 days with the option to extend. For long-term living it's more convenient to arrange a 5-year DTV visa.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live on Samui?
faq.answer: Comparable to Phuket: slightly pricier than mainland Thailand because of island logistics. See the exact budget in the calculator above.

faq.question: What language is spoken on Samui?
faq.answer: Thai; English is widely used in tourist areas, and Russian also turns up in the service sector.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card on Samui?
faq.answer: No, Russian cards don't work. You'll need baht in cash and a card from a foreign bank.

faq.question: What is the climate like on Samui?
faq.answer: Tropical: hot year-round, with the main rainy season from October to December.

faq.question: How do I get to Samui?
faq.answer: Via Bangkok: a domestic flight to the island, or a bus and ferry. There are no direct flights from Russia.

reviews.text: I moved from Phuket — Samui is quieter and greener. I live on a DTV, work remotely, and the beach is five minutes away by scooter. The downside is that I flew to Bangkok for serious healthcare.
An island for those who want the sea and tranquillity. The community is warm and the food is amazing. The rainy season can be gloomy, but in winter it's paradise.
